column1: ## Round-3 held-out benchmark -- ratings (2026-10-16; re-rated 2026-10-16 after the fix round).
## 107 inputs the engine had never been tuned against (64 captured, 43
## reproduced; provenance in manifest.tsv), rated on round 2's criteria,
## reused unchanged and frozen in CRITERIA.md BEFORE the first input was run.
## Engine: main at the 2.1.0 release (eacc9fa), after the 2026-10-14 parser
##   PASS     everything present AND correctly structured
##   PARTIAL  broadly right; something lost or mis-shaped
##   FAIL     the output misrepresents the input
## strategy/conf  the default-mode winner (--max-strategies 1, confidence rank)
## cov            its line coverage (%), the 4th field of --emit-meta ("-" when
## prio           the --rank priority winner; "=" means the same strategy, and
##                the output was byte-identical (cmp) in every such case
## rating         default mode, judged on the melted tidy table (run.sh --tidy);
## multi          `provost --multi` relative to default: same / better / worse
##                ("same" includes the 59 inputs whose single --multi dataset is
##                byte-identical to the default tidy table)
## family         the shape family the write-up aggregates by
## cluster        the defect cluster ("-" for PASS)
## Columns input .. note are the rating on 2.1.0, unchanged. The six columns
## after them are the 2026-10-16 re-rating on the engine after the fix round
## that followed (CHANGELOG, the three 2026-10-16 engine entries: format parsers
## that decline, section-tables and indentation as depth; the gutter grid's
## UTF-8 offsets, headerless rows, footers and banners; column-type consistency
## and its hold). Default mode, same criteria and rules. The fix round's agents
## never saw these inputs: the round was built, frozen and rated first.
## strategy_1016/conf_1016  the default-mode winner on that engine
## cov_1016       its line coverage (%), the 4th field of --emit-meta
## cons_1016      its column-type consistency (%), the 5th field of --emit-meta
##                ("-" when no column could be judged, or nothing was extracted)
## rating_1016    default-mode rating; prio_rating / multi were NOT re-rated
## note_1016      "=" when the default tidy output is byte-identical (cmp) to
##                the 2.1.0 run, so the rating carries over; else what changed
## Since this re-rating the set has been looked at: it measures REGRESSION, not
## generalisation (see the postscript of the round-3 report). The next honest
## Self-assessment by an agent, as in rounds 1 and 2: a screen, not a verdict.
## The moment anyone tunes the engine against these files they stop measuring
## generalisation -- update the ratings in the same commit and say so here.
